builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Compression Through a Context Lens: Evaluating Adaptation, Quantization, and Distillation in Arabic Legal LLMs
summary: The technique replaces full-precision model weights (typically 16-bit) with 4-bit weights, and replaces a monolithic large teacher with a smaller distilled student if needed. It costs a small amount of accuracy (no-context drops of up to 3.2 percentage points for quantization, and generally declining accuracy with smaller distilled students) and adds deployment pipeline complexity. After adoption, the reliance on full-context prompting can mask internal knowledge collapse, meaning performance can fail unexpectedly when legal context is absent from the input.
rationale: The reader operates under a single 24 GB GPU constraint, making a 64-71% memory reduction via 4-bit quantization immediately actionable, highly cost-effective, and proven to have minimal accuracy loss.
technique: 4-bit Quantization and Distillation for Legal LLMs

claims.statement: The technique replaces full-precision model weights (typically 16-bit) with 4-bit weights, and replaces a monolithic large teacher with a smaller distilled student if needed. It costs a small amount of accuracy (no-context drops of up to 3.2 percentage points for quantization, and generally declining accuracy with smaller distilled students) and adds deployment pipeline complexity. After adoption, the reliance on full-context prompting can mask internal knowledge collapse, meaning performance can fail unexpectedly when legal context is absent from the input.
Four-bit quantization reduces model memory by 64-71% (a ~2.78x to 3.45x footprint reduction), with changes in no-context MCQ accuracy ranging from -3.2 to +1.6 percentage points.
